answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 48 px wide in all 64 rows, so it is a full tile block. Rows 0-47 are one vertical, front-facing earth/stone texture panel framed by two narrow side strips. These strips have small grass tufts at rows 0-2 and end in a dark base line at row 47. The column scans show only scattered 1-row light speckles (L=140) over the texture. They are noise, not a front-edge line with eave shadow, and no band of rows forms a sloped plane. Nothing reads as an inclined ramp surface receding upward. Rows 48-63 are flat ground with the same speckled texture and no ramp edge line. There is no ellipse, no roof plane and no visible contents. The ramp therefore reads as a flat front elevation of a wall, not a three-quarter view with a foreshortened top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's earthen ramp shows about 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. The ramp face has horizontal plank bands, vertical grain, and speckle on the sandy foot, with a small green grass cap at the top. There are no large flat areas. The ramp is a little less textured than the paving reference, and the side posts are fairly uniform vertical strips. Overall it is at least as rich as the references on the measured facts and sits acceptably next to them.
